key_insight: Concept-based explanations in AI may look human-friendly, but they are not automatically reliable. ConceptSMILE extends perturbation-based auditing to check whether concept-level explanations truly reflect model behavior.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of trustworthy evaluation methods for concept-based explainable AI, where explanations can be interpretable but still misleading, unstable, or unfaithful to the model.
method: Introduces ConceptSMILE, a model-agnostic auditing framework built on perturbation-based evaluation.
Extends the SMILE idea from feature- or region-level attribution to human-understandable concept explanations.
Assesses whether changes to input perturbations produce explanation responses that are consistent with trustworthy concept-level reasoning.
impact: This gives AI/ML practitioners a practical way to audit concept-based XAI methods before using them in high-stakes settings. It helps ensure explanations are not just understandable, but also reliable and faithful to the model.

paper_title: ConceptSMILE: Auditing the Trustworthiness of Concept-Based Explainable AI
paper_authors: Mohadeseh Mollapour, Koorosh Aslansefat, Zeinab Dehghani, Bhupesh Kumar Mishra, Tejal Shah
